distinguishing_features: Applies thermal-fatigue mitigation to PCB solder interconnects under CTE-mismatch power cycling rather than turbine-liner cracking.
Uses passive spatial redistribution of heat/current across multiple parallel solder joints instead of sensor-derived thermodynamic inference and active duty capping.
Requires a four-pad solder array and modified lead frame so each joint is asserted to carry a fraction of the component power.
Validates by comparing two-joint and four-joint boards and requiring a 75% drop in measured solder-joint ΔT.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce cyclic thermo-mechanical fatigue damage in power-cycled PCB solder interconnects by lowering the local thermal excursion and strain experienced by each joint.
parsed.viable_reason: The candidate treats solder joints as parallel heat loads whose local ΔT equals P/k times Rth, but CTE-mismatch fatigue is governed by assembly differential-expansion strain and global thermal excursion, and the stated external thermal-cycle test would impose the same ΔT on both boards, so the claimed 75% reduction is not physically supported.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Once the goal is to lower the thermal-fatigue driver, adding more pads and parallel lead-frame paths is a routine PCB load-sharing design measure, while prior art 1 already teaches reducing peak thermal load to mitigate thermal fatigue.
